title: How a Mechanical Watch Keeps Time With ZERO Batteries

stage.note: Scene uses stage.safeBox() to ensure all content is visible in both portrait (1080x1920) and landscape (1920x1080) orientations

narration_script.text: Zero batteries. Zero microchips. Yet this coiled strip of steel counts six hundred ninety-one thousand exact beats every single day.
Remove one tiny part... and all that stored energy explodes out in half a second.
So engineers lock it behind a mechanical gate called the escapement.
Slow time down fifty times. Watch the ruby fork trap the gear... releasing just one tooth per swing.
That rhythm comes from the balance wheel, breathing back and forth eight times every second.
Now watch the gear train turn those eight tiny ticks... into seconds, minutes, and hours.

simplifications: Escape wheel has 15 teeth (real Swiss lever has 15-21). Simplified geometry.
Gear train ratios are visually representative, not exact watchmaking ratios.
Hairspring is a flat spiral (real Breguet overcoil omitted for clarity).
Movement plate shown as single layer (real movements have multiple plates and bridges).
